behaviors.invariant: Search matches eligible name, profile, and email fields with the right score and visibility.
behaviors.reason: A wrong match or score makes people difficult to find or exposes an ineligible match.

tests.reason: The matcher owns field eligibility; this theory tests distinct bio fields.
The matcher owns relevance scoring across exact and partial names.
This pins the visibility boundary at the matching owner.
It rechecks matching semantics already owned by PersonSearchMatcher; the adapter's field projection can be checked alongside its name case.
It repeats the matcher's bio-field decision without a distinct cache or adapter assertion.
One simple end-to-end adapter case proves that search results are produced from cached users.
The service must preserve the matcher's score in HumanSearchResult.
The adapter must carry the matched address and result metadata to callers.

behaviors.invariant: Search filters cached people and resolves pasted IDs without returning rejected profiles or merge tombstones.
behaviors.reason: A result may identify the wrong account or return a person who must not appear in search.

tests.reason: The service filters ordinary search results before calling the matcher.
The ID fast path bypasses the ordinary matcher and needs its own negative case.
The cache must suppress archived IDs during ordinary matching.
A pasted archived ID must resolve to its live survivor.
An ExactName query with GUID syntax must remain a name lookup.

behaviors.invariant: A queued message is delivered once, marked sent, and sending is paced according to the throttle.
behaviors.reason: Incorrect order or cancellation handling can duplicate an accepted email; real-time waiting makes the suite slow.

tests.reason: Keep the delivery and sent-state assertions; avoid paying a real one-second post-send delay.
The batch boundary matters, but ten successful sends cost ten real seconds with the present throttle.

behaviors.invariant: Cancellation after the transport accepts a message cannot make that message retryable.
behaviors.reason: Cancellation during the post-send delay must not flip a sent message to Failed and queue a duplicate.

tests.reason: Cancellation at the throttle boundary must propagate while the saved message remains Sent.

behaviors.invariant: Retention deletes only sent messages older than the configured cutoff while preserving daily counts.
behaviors.reason: Deleting queued or failed mail loses delivery attempts; deleting counts corrupts reporting.

tests.reason: The repository owns the age and status predicate.
The service owns the configured cutoff passed to the repository.
Daily counts must survive email retention.
It repeats the repository's status predicate through a service with no additional branch for failed mail.
It repeats the repository's status predicate through a service with no additional branch for queued mail.
It repeats the repository's age predicate; the service cutoff case remains.

behaviors.invariant: An explicit Reply-To address is saved with the queued message.
behaviors.reason: A lost Reply-To prevents a recipient's response from reaching the sender.

tests.reason: This checks the saved Reply-To along with recipient identity and lookup behavior.
The other test already checks the same persisted field on the same send path.

behaviors.invariant: Register reads share a cached snapshot and derive slug, ID, and membership results from it.
behaviors.reason: The existing Workgroups tests construct the undecorated inner service; the decorator needs one focused cache-hit assertion.

tests.reason: A repeated register read must avoid a second inner load.

behaviors.invariant: A write clears the cached register even if later inner work throws after persisting.
behaviors.reason: Without failure-path invalidation, a partial write can leave members or coordinators seeing stale state.

tests.reason: A successful write must forward the right IDs and clear the warmed snapshot.
A write that throws after changing data still requires cache invalidation.
